questions.title: Newey-West Bartlett HAC inference for a stationary mean
questions.description: Focused integrated L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Newey and West (1987), DOI 10.2307/1913610, and a pinned statsmodels Bartlett-HAC implementation excerpt. Let Y_1,...,Y_n be a finite segment of an equally spaced covariance-stationary scalar process with mean mu and autocovariance gamma(k)=Cov(Y_t,Y_{t-k}). In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX workspace, derive the exact finite-n identity for Var(sqrt(n)(bar Y_n-mu)), identify the population long-run variance Omega=gamma(0)+2 sum_{k>=1} gamma(k), and state explicit dependence, moment, autocovariance-summability, bandwidth, and CLT conditions sufficient for asymptotic normal inference. For a supplied integer L, define centered sample autocovariances gamma_hat_k=n^{-1} sum_{t=k+1}^n (Y_t-bar Y_n)(Y_{t-k}-bar Y_n), Bartlett weights w_k=1-k/(L+1), and Omega_hat_L=gamma_hat_0+2 sum_{k=1}^L w_k gamma_hat_k. Derive this exact convention, establish its nonnegativity through a valid finite-sample argument, and distinguish the finite sample estimator from Omega, finite-sample unbiasedness, and asymptotic consistency when L=L_n grows. Specialize the population calculation to a stationary Gaussian AR(1), Y_t-mu=phi(Y_{t-1}-mu)+epsilon_t with |phi|<1 and innovation variance sigma_e^2, obtaining gamma(0), Omega, and the factor by which an iid standard error misses the asymptotic variance. Discuss negative as well as positive phi. The required model-authored Python artifact is est_newey_west_mean and must implement the frozen run_estimator(request) contract exactly. It may use NumPy but must not call a prebuilt HAC routine. Exploratory Python or R may compare the implementation with direct matrix calculations and inspect finite AR(1) behavior. A separately frozen confirmatory experiment uses predeclared Gaussian AR(1) designs, bandwidths fixed before candidate execution, independent exact formula checks, long-run variance accuracy, and normal-interval coverage with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Such simulation supports only those finite designs and is not proof. Source-code replication and novelty are not required, and Lean formalization is not applicable.

primary_paper.title: A Simple, Positive Semi-Definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix

implementation_convention.title: statsmodels Bartlett HAC implementation
implementation_convention.meaning: The model-visible excerpt fixes the Bartlett weight and lag-sum convention; the public estimator contract below is the executable authority.

request_fields.name: observations
request_fields.meaning: One finite, equally spaced scalar time-series segment in chronological order.
request_fields.indexing: zero-based chronological order; missing periods are not admitted
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, nested values, nonfinite values, and fewer than twelve observations; do not reorder or coerce entries.

request_fields.name: max_lag
request_fields.meaning: The fixed highest included autocovariance lag L, selected before inspecting this request's outcomes.
request_fields.indexing: lag zero is always included and positive lags run through L
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonintegers, negative values, and values above n-2; do not choose or modify the lag internally.

response_fields.name: n_observations
response_fields.meaning: The number n of supplied observations.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be a native JSON integer and must not count any padded or omitted value.

response_fields.name: max_lag
response_fields.meaning: The exact lag L supplied in the request.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must preserve the request exactly and must not report an automatically selected bandwidth.

response_fields.name: sample_mean
response_fields.meaning: The arithmetic mean of the supplied observations.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be a native JSON-finite number.

response_fields.name: autocovariances
response_fields.meaning: The centered divisor-n sample autocovariances gamma_hat_k for lags zero through L.
response_fields.indexing: entry k is n^{-1} sum_{t=k+1}^n (Y_t-bar Y)(Y_{t-k}-bar Y)
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not divide by n-k or n-1, do not omit lag zero, and do not circularly wrap the series.
response_fields.normalization: Every lag sum uses the common divisor n.

response_fields.name: bartlett_weights
response_fields.meaning: The Bartlett weights for lags zero through L.
response_fields.edge_cases: The lag-zero value is one and the lag-L value is 1/(L+1); do not use 1-k/L.

response_fields.name: long_run_variance
response_fields.meaning: The finite-sample Bartlett HAC estimate Omega_hat_L.
response_fields.shape: one finite nonnegative scalar up to floating-point roundoff
response_fields.indexing: aggregates returned lags zero through L
response_fields.edge_cases: Must use the returned centered divisor-n autocovariances and supplied L; a tiny negative roundoff no smaller than -1e-12 may be clipped to zero, but a materially negative value is invalid.

response_fields.name: mean_standard_error
response_fields.meaning: The HAC standard-error estimate for the sample mean.
response_fields.edge_cases: May equal zero for a constant series; do not apply a Student-t or degrees-of-freedom multiplier.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly observations and max_lag, and the response contains exactly n_observations, max_lag, sample_mean, autocovariances, bartlett_weights, long_run_variance, and mean_standard_error. Missing, extra, malformed, coercible-only, or nonfinite values are rejected.

The response uses the exact divisor-n centered autocovariances and Bartlett weights, long_run_variance equals their declared weighted sum, and mean_standard_error squared equals long_run_variance/n up to floating-point tolerance.
When max_lag is zero, bartlett_weights is [1], long_run_variance is the divisor-n centered sample variance, and mean_standard_error is its square root divided by sqrt(n).
Adding a finite constant c to every observation adds c to sample_mean and leaves autocovariances, bartlett_weights, long_run_variance, and mean_standard_error unchanged.

Multiplying every observation by a finite nonzero scalar a multiplies sample_mean by a, every autocovariance and long_run_variance by a^2, leaves Bartlett weights unchanged, and multiplies mean_standard_error by abs(a).
Reversing the finite observation order leaves every returned quantity unchanged under this two-sided scalar Bartlett convention.

empirical_claims.meaning: For every frozen input, the candidate outputs agree with an independent direct lag-sum implementation and the exact public transformations under predeclared numerical tolerances.

Across predeclared stationary Gaussian AR(1) designs with positive, zero, and negative dependence, the candidate HAC estimate is compared with the known population Omega=sigma_e^2/(1-phi)^2 using bandwidths fixed before candidate execution and Monte Carlo uncertainty.
The frozen assessment records normal-interval coverage for mu using the candidate HAC standard error and reports Monte Carlo uncertainty; it does not require exact finite-sample 95 percent coverage.
Finite AR(1) experiments and source agreement are computational evidence only; they do not prove positive semidefiniteness, consistency, a CLT, or validity for arbitrary stationary processes.
